instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express — positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the author's own feeling, including excitement about upcoming plans, praise, or pride (positive), versus annoyance, disappointment, insults, or bad news framed as bad (negative). Factual reports, schedules, sales offers, questions, and wry observations without clear feeling are neutral, even when they mention dates, rankings, or controversial topics. Mild sarcasm or jokes count as neutral unless they clearly attack or complain; reported negative events (scandals, sobbing asylum seeker, slow economy) lean negative.

neutral.what: Informational, factual, or offhand tweets: scores, schedules, news headlines, sales, questions, random facts, mild ironic remarks with no clear emotional stance.
examples: Anyone wanna buy a Zac Brown Band ticket for the 3rd?
David Wright is 6 for 20 with 5 walks in five games with St. Lucie.
I'm not sure what Rahul Gandhi is trying to accomplish with all of this
neutral.cues: selling, scheduled, kicks off, random fact, reportedly, game stats, dates, 'may' speculation
neutral.not_for: Factual headlines about clearly bad events or scandals (negative); announcements with excitement markers (positive).

positive.what: Author shows enjoyment, anticipation, praise, pride, congratulations, or excitement, including about plans for tomorrow/weekend or achievements.
examples: Living for Magic Mike XXL with @user tomorrow.
8th strikeout of the afternoon for David Price's 100th career win!
I think I'm gonna wear leggings tomorrow with my Jurassic Park shirt pls send clothing advice
positive.cues: excited, can't wait, proud, great, love, YES!!, Happy, Congratulations, Good deal, YUM, !!!
positive.not_for: Plain ticket sales or event announcements without enthusiasm (neutral); 'RIP'-style jokes may still be positive if affection shown.

negative.what: Author complains, insults, mocks, expresses frustration, disappointment, fear, or reports clearly bad news or failures.
examples: 2nd time going to Dunkin today and there closed. Like no this is not ok
Obama is putting US on par with every other 3rd world country
Slow Economic Gains in 3rd Quarter: ABJ - October 26 - Some reason for optimism surfaced during the third-quarte...
negative.cues: sucks, worse, bad, shite, bullshit, pissed, CRY, scared, cancelled, can't go, disaster, shameful, asshole
negative.not_for: Neutral-toned observations with 'lol' or mild irony (neutral); profanity used in excitement like 'pissed' celebrating (positive).
